scenes.title: Yvonne Godard, nageuse
scenes.description: A press photograph of the swimmer Yvonne Godard, taken by the Mondial Photo-Presse agency and distributed by Agence Mondial in Paris in 1932. The record identifies it as a portrait of a swimmer in France, held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
scenes.explanation: Angled starting block wedges for swimmers were not introduced until the 1970s, so this object cannot exist in a 1932 pool.

scenes.title: Celebration at the Exhibition Centre
scenes.description: A photograph taken on 4 June 1942 at Juhla Messukeskuksessa. The record does not state who took it.
scenes.anomaly: modern clip-on LED music stand light
scenes.explanation: Clip-on LED music stand lights with bright white LEDs did not exist in 1942; battery-powered stand lights of the era used dim incandescent bulbs.

scenes.title: Risør. Indre Havn.
scenes.description: A photograph of the inner harbour in Risør, held by the National Library of Norway and in the public domain, dated 1900. The record does not name a photographer.
scenes.explanation: A compact clamp-on outboard motor could not exist in this 1900 harbour scene, because the first practical outboard motors were only introduced in 1906.
scenes.credit: Mittet & Co. AS via National Library of Norway

scenes.title: Portuguese cavalry descending a steep slope
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol showing Portuguese cavalry coming down a steep slope. It is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France (Gallica) and dated 1911.
scenes.explanation: Molded plastic safety helmets of this rounded-shell type did not exist in 1911; industrial head protection then used leather or cloth caps.

scenes.title: Independence Day Celebration
scenes.description: The photograph shows soldiers standing in ranks in a field during a celebration. It was taken at Marjoniemen kentällä in 1959.
scenes.explanation: Digital LCD stopwatches did not exist in 1959; the first digital stopwatches appeared in the 1970s.
